item.text: {"question_id":"3B.1","answer":"In 2023, protection was materially inadequate and mixed. The government promulgated victim-protection and reparations frameworks, enacted laws concerning human-rights defenders and penitentiary principles, supported justice and police-reform measures, and reported investigations and prosecutions of security personnel (BATCH-0009-E004; BATCH-0011-E003; BATCH-0029-E001; BATCH-0029-E002; BATCH-0019-E001). These formal measures and some convictions show partial protective and corrective capacity, but do not establish nationwide enforcement or effective remedy. Credible reporting documented government or security-force arbitrary killings, enforced disappearances, torture or cruel treatment, arbitrary detention, political detainees, harsh prisons, and routine violations of arrest safeguards; authorities also restricted access to some intelligence and military detention facilities, while impunity remained serious (BATCH-0011-E009). In Goma, security forces reportedly killed 56 demonstrators, arrested 158 people, and later prosecuted both civilians and security personnel. Although some officers were convicted and reparations were ordered, Amnesty found incomplete investigations, flawed prosecutions, unresolved victim identification, restricted participation, and inaccessible appeals (BATCH-0011-E009; BATCH-0011-E021). The release of Franck Diongo without charge is a corrective outcome, but the supplied evidence gives no reason for the arrest and no evidence of discipline or remedy for responsible officials; it therefore does not establish effective protection (BATCH-0003-E007). Some severe violence was committed by armed groups or arose from conflict conditions, so it cannot be personally attributed to Tshisekedi without further evidence. Overall, the 2023 record supports recurring state-attributed abuse with partial accountability and weak remedy, alongside meaningful but incompletely implemented legal and institutional
